heroLead: Fredericktown sits along the Monongahela across from California, PA, in a stretch of Washington County where coal and gas history run side by side.
intro: Fredericktown is a small Washington County community on the Monongahela River, close to California, PA on the opposite bank. Like much of the river corridor through this county, land here has a mining and gas history that stretches back well before Marcellus, and title records often reflect both.
We buy mineral and royalty interests near Fredericktown, whether your family's interest is producing under a modern lease or traces back to an older, smaller-scale gas agreement.

sections.heading: River-corridor mineral history
paragraphs: Land along the Monongahela in this part of Washington County changed hands through mining, river commerce, and farming over more than a century, and mineral rights were frequently severed from the surface at different points along the way.

sections.heading: Marcellus activity in this stretch
paragraphs: Washington County overall sits in the wet-gas core of the Marcellus play, though development density varies along the river corridor compared to the county's interior townships, so we look at the specific tract's position relative to active units.

sections.heading: What we need to review your interest
paragraphs: Any deed, lease, or royalty statement you have helps, but we can also start from a parcel description and pull county records directly.
We're comfortable working with incomplete files, since that's the norm rather than the exception for river-corridor land with this much layered history.

faqs.question: Is Fredericktown in the core Marcellus wet-gas area?
faqs.answer: It's within Washington County's wet-gas fairway, though development density along the river corridor here can differ from the county's interior townships, so tract-specific review matters.

faqs.question: My family's Fredericktown land has old mining history. Does that complicate an oil and gas sale?
faqs.answer: It can complicate the title work since mineral rights were often severed at different points in this river corridor's history, but it doesn't typically prevent a sale — we just confirm what's actually being conveyed.

faqs.question: Do you buy interests on both sides of the Monongahela near Fredericktown?
faqs.answer: Yes, we review mineral interests throughout this area regardless of which side of the river the tract sits on.

faqs.question: Is my Fredericktown-area interest affected by activity happening on the California, PA side of the river?
faqs.answer: Not directly for ownership purposes, since Pennsylvania mineral title follows the recorded deed for your specific tract, but nearby activity on either bank can still be a useful signal of overall development trends in the corridor.
